articles.title: Nuevo ataque machista a una tenista: "Espero que te suicides, no estarás a la altura de un hombre, perra"
articles.standfirst: La tenista Jodie Burrage denuncia ante la WTA los despreciables ataques que ha sufrido tras su regreso al circuito
articles.summary: La tenista Jodie Burrage denuncia ante la WTA los despreciables ataques que ha sufrido tras su regreso al circuito
articles.body: La Jodie Burrage ha revelado que ha recibido amenazas de muerte en redes sociales tras disputar su primer partido en el circuito WTA después de 16 meses de ausencia. La tenista británica, que es la número 474 del ránking, fue derrotada en la primera ronda en Chennai por la india Vaishnavi Adkar por 3-6, 6-3, 7-5. Tras la derrota Jodie Burrage (27 años) compartió en su 'stories' de Instagram los ataques que sufrió en redes sociales y los compartió con la WTA. "¡Qué buena bienvenida a mi regreso al circuito! Ya recuerdo por qué me fui. ¿Cuándo van a hacer algo al respecto?", denunció la tenista británica. Algunos de los mensajes más despreciables que sufrió Burrage fueron "eres una cobarde que tira la toalla. De verdad, eres una vergüenza para este deporte. Hoy te han dado una paliza, y eres precisamente la razón por la que el deporte femenino es un chiste", "espero que te vayas a casa y te suicides, porque, sinceramente, es lo mejor que puedes hacer. Nunca estarás a la altura de un hombre, perra" o "muérete y provoca disturbios en las calles". La denuncia de Burrage, número 15 de Gran Bretaña, se produce más de un año después de que otra tenista británica, Katie Boulter, confesara haber recibido también amenazas de muerte a través de las redes sociales. En 2025 Katie Boulter recibió mensajes como "espero que te dé cáncer", "profanaremos la tumba de tu abuela si no está muerta para mañana" o "vete al infierno; he perdido el dinero que me envió mi madre".

articles.title: Hong Kong Open: GB's Mika Stojsavljevic, 17, beats Sofia Kenin for first WTA Tour main-draw win
articles.summary: British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic beats former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin for her first WTA Tour main-draw win.
articles.body:
British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic beat former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin to claim her first WTA Tour main-draw win - despite only having an hour's notice that she would be playing.

The 17-year-old lost in qualifying for the Hong Kong Open but entered the main draw as a lucky loser.

World number 411 Stojsavljevic came through a close deciding set to beat the American 6-3 4-6 6-4.

"I only knew an hour before I was going to be playing. I kind of just went out and swung today," Stojsavljevic said.

"I know she's a Grand Slam champion and it was never going to be an easy match, but I believed in myself and it worked out."

Kenin, 27, has had a torrid time since winning the Melbourne title in 2020 but is still ranked 224 places above the Briton.

Stojsavljevic hit six winners to her opponent's zero and saved three of the eight break points she faced.

It is a second big win of the year for Stojsavljevic, who stunned then world number 56 Talia Gibson at Billie Jean King Cup qualifying in April.

Stojsavljevic started playing tennis aged seven at Ealing Lawn Tennis Club in north-west London after watching her brother practise.

In 2024, she became the first Briton in 15 years to win the US Open junior title.

She reached a high of fifth in the junior world rankings and turned professional in 2025.

Earlier this year, she reached the quarter-finals of the WTA 125 event in Birmingham - the tier that sits below the main Tour.

Stojsavljevic will face world number 67 Zeynep Sonmez in the second round in Hong Kong.

Fellow Briton Katie Boulter's season came to an end with a 7-5 6-4 loss to American Claire Liu at the same tournament.

articles.title: British No. 15 Jodie Burrage reveals horrific social media death threats after losing to India's Vaishnavi Adkar on 16-month WTA return
articles.summary: Jodie Burrage, British tennis player, reveals she received death threats on social media following her defeat at the Chennai Open, sparking outrage and calls for action against online abuse in sports.
articles.body: British tennis player Jodie Burrage has revealed that she received death threats and abusive messages after losing her first WTA Tour singles match in 16 months. The 27-year-old shared screenshots of the messages after her first-round defeat at the Chennai Open, questioning why social media platforms had not done more to protect players.Jodie Burrage shares death threats after Chennai Open defeatBurrage, ranked 474th in the world and Britain's No 15, lost 3-6, 6-3, 7-5 to India's Vaishnavi Adkar in the first round of the Chennai Open. Despite taking the opening set, the British player was unable to prevent Adkar from recovering to win the match in three sets.It was Burrage's first match in the main draw of a WTA Tour event since July 2025, excluding qualifying tournaments. Her previous appearance at that level had ended in a first-round defeat by Catherine McNally at Wimbledon.After the Chennai match, Burrage posted an Instagram story showing a scroll of direct messages she had received. Alongside the video, she wrote: “Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left. When will something be done?”She tagged both the WTA and Instagram, directing attention to the abuse and asking what action would be taken against those sending it.One message accused Burrage of being a “quitter” and a “disgrace to the sport”, before attacking women's tennis and telling her to kill herself. It read: “Your [sic] a quitter smh [shake my head]. You truly are a disgrace to the sport. You got your ass whooped today and you are the exact reason women's sports are a joke.“Hope you go home and kill yourself bc [because] honestly that's what's best. You will never compare to a man b***h.”Another pending direct message read: “Die n riot [sic] on the streets”, while a separate message directed at the player said: “F***** [sic] ****”.The messages included personal abuse and encouragement of self-harm, rather than criticism of Burrage's performance. Her post also drew support from fellow players, including Germany's Eva Lys, who shared the issue on Instagram and tagged the WTA, asking: “When will something be done?”Katie Boulter also received death threats after French Open matchBurrage's experience follows a similar case involving fellow British player Katie Boulter, who spoke to BBC Sport in 2025 about receiving death threats and other abusive messages online.Boulter became the target of abuse after losing the first set of her opening-round match against Carole Monnet at the French Open. She went on to win the match, but the result did not prevent users from sending threats to her social media accounts.Screenshots shown to the BBC included one message saying: “Hope you get cancer”. Another threatened to damage her grandmother's grave if she was not dead by the following day, while also referring to “candles and a coffin for your entire family”.A third message read: “Go to hell, I lost money my mother sent me.”The reference to lost money reflected a pattern identified in research into online abuse directed at tennis players. A report by the Signify Group, which monitors threats and abuse through its AI-led threat detection service, found two years ago that angry gamblers were responsible for 48 per cent of posts classified as abusive.More than 12,000 abusive messages targeted female tennis players in 2025The scale of the problem extends beyond individual cases. According to a report published earlier in 2026, female tennis players received more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media during 2025.According to the BBC, data from the Signify Group's threat matrix service showed that the number of abusive posts and messages was similar to the figure recorded in 2024. The report also found that angry gamblers accounted for 42 per cent of verified abuse in 2025 and 59 per cent of cases classified as serious abuse.The findings point to gambling-related anger as a significant source of online hostility towards players, although the abuse received by Burrage and Boulter also included threats and misogynistic attacks unrelated to any assessment of their performances.Players have previously called for social media companies to introduce identity verification measures in an effort to make users more accountable for the messages they send. The WTA's player board has also condemned the abuse, describing it as “unacceptable” and warning that its impact on those targeted can be “significant”.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Real Madrid: Rafael Nadal appointed to LaLiga club's board of directors
articles.summary: Real Madrid hailed retired tennis great Rafael Nadal, as they announced the 22-time Grand Slam champion would be joining the club's board of directors
articles.body:
The club expressed its pride at the news the 22-time Grand Slam champion, and longtime Real Madrid fan, had taken the executive role on Wednesday.

Following the announcement, Nadal published a photo of himself as a child wearing a Real Madrid kit on his X account.

"I want to thank president Florentino Perez and the board who proposed me to be part of the board of directors at Real Madrid," Nadal wrote in the caption.

"I accepted this proposal with great excitement, a desire to learn and contribute everything I can."

It comes after Nadal, an honorary member of Real Madrid, took to social media earlier in 2026 to deny reports linking him to a possible candidacy for the club's presidency as "untrue".

Following Wednesday's announcement, Real Madrid paid homage to the 40-year-old, who retired from professional tennis in 2024, explaining Nadal's values aligned with the club's.

"Rafael Nadal, an honorary member of Real Madrid, is one of the greatest legends in the history of sport and one of the most admired and recognised Spanish athletes in the world," a club spokesperson said.

"For Real Madrid and for all Madrid fans, it is a great source of pride that a figure of his sporting and human stature, a benchmark of Spanish and world sport, will become part of our Board of Directors and contribute, from this position of responsibility, to the present and future of our club.

"Rafael Nadal has forged a legendary sporting career. But his figure represents much more than his successes: his talent, his constant drive to improve, his capacity for sacrifice, his competitiveness, his humility, his respect for rivals and team-mates, and his commitment to solidarity make him an example both on and off the court.

"All these values ​​are part of Real Madrid's identity, and Rafael Nadal has represented and defended them throughout his sporting life, becoming a role model for millions of people around the world."

images.caption: Image: Real Madrid have appointed Rafael Nadal to its board of directors

articles.title: Mika Stojsavljevic: British teenager earns first WTA Tour win, beating Sofia Kenin in Hong Kong after only an hour's notice
articles.summary: Mika Stojsavljevic defeats 2020 Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin after being restored to tournament as a lucky loser; seventeen-year-old overcomes ranking gap of over 200 places; Stojsavljevic's fellow Brit Katie Boulter knocked out in second round, watch WTA Tour live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The 17-year-old was given a spot as a lucky loser at the Hong Kong Open when Leylah Fernandez - runner-up to Emma Raudcanu at the 2021 US Open - withdrew.

Stojsavljevic, the world No 411, overcame a rankings gap of over 200 places as she beat Kenin 6-3 4-6 6-4 to set up a second-round meeting with Turkey's Zeynep Sönmez.

Stojsavljevic, who lost in the first round of qualifying in Hong Kong before her reprieve, said: "I only knew an hour before that I was going to be playing. I kind of just went out and swung. We didn't have much time to prepare.

"Obviously, I know she's a Grand Slam champion so it was never going to be an easy match but I believed in myself and it worked out."

Stojsavljevic lost her way from a set and 3-0 up against American Kenin but rebounded to win the deciding set in a match in which she struck six aces, six winners and converted six of 13 break points.

In 2024, the Londoner became the first Brit in 15 years to win the US Open girls' title, following Heather Watson's triumph back in 2009.

Stojsavljevic made her Billie Jean King Cup debut for Great Britain against Australia in Melbourne in April, defeating current world No 36 Talia Gibson in straight sets.

Elsewhere in Hong Kong on Wednesday, Stojsavljevic's compatriot Katie Boulter saw her season come to an end with a 7-5 6-4 defeat to American Claire Liu.

If Stojsavljevic is able to overcome Sönmez, she will play Liu in round three.

British No 1 Boulter had beaten Viktorija Golubic in straight sets in round one, despite an incident that "got under her skin".

articles.title: Dani Mérida se despide de París y de la temporada 2026
articles.standfirst: El madrileño cede ante Tommy Paul en el que era su último torneo del curso
articles.summary: El madrileño cede ante Tommy Paul en el que era su último torneo del curso
articles.body: Dani Mérida puede estar más que satisfecho con su 2026. El tenista de la capital ha cedido ante el estadounidense Tommy Paul por 6-1 y 6-1 en la segunda ronda del Masters 1000 de París, el que era la última cita de su calendario. Dani, que pasó con nota su debut en el TMS galo ante el argentino Sebastián Baez, hoy no ha podido con la maquinaria de Paul sobre pista cubierta. El americano necesitó 23 minutos para apuntarse la primera manga, en la que tan solo dejó escapar cuatro puntos. En el segundo set, una rotura en el juego inicial terminó de dibujar el camino en la pista 2 de la Défense Arena de París. Finalmente no jugará en Estocolmo la semana del 7 al 14 de este mes. Por lo tanto, el madrileño no volverá a competir hasta 2027. El español ha colmado una temporada llena de buenas noticias. Consiguió estrenar su palmarés alzándose con el ATP 250 de Umag; alcanzó la mejor posición de su carrera, subiendo hasta el escalón número 39 del ranking; y ya sabe lo que es jugar bajo los colores de su país en la Copa Davis, consiguiendo una victoria de mucho mérito ante el chileno Alejandro Tabilo en su propia tierra.

articles.title: Tennis great Rafael Nadal set to join Real Madrid board
articles.summary: The 22-time Grand Slam winner is to be ratified onto club’s board of directors.
articles.body:
Real Madrid are set to add a champion from another ⁠sporting arena to ⁠their boardroom as 22-time tennis Grand Slam winner Rafael Nadal’s appointment as a director is to be put to members for ⁠ratification, the club says.

The board agreed to submit the appointment to the General Assembly of ⁠Delegated Members. Nadal is already an honorary member of the club.

“It is a source of immense pride for Real Madrid and for all our supporters that a figure of his sporting and personal stature … is to join ‌our Board of Directors,” Real said in a statement on Wednesday.

The club highlighted Nadal’s sporting achievements, including 92 singles titles, two Olympic gold medals, five Davis Cup triumphs with Spain and the world number one ranking.

The club said his qualities beyond those honours – including humility, respect for opponents and commitment to charity – mirrored the club’s own.

“All ⁠these values form part of Real Madrid’s identity, and ⁠Rafael Nadal has embodied and championed them throughout his sporting career,” said the statement announcing his appointment at a board meeting on Tuesday.

“I would like to thank President Florentino Perez and the Board for ⁠inviting me to join the Board of Directors of Real Madrid,” he wrote on social media.

“I have ⁠accepted this invitation with great enthusiasm, keen to ⁠learn and to contribute as much as I can.”

Nadal, who retired from tennis in November 2024, has long been touted as a potential successor to Perez, ‌although he has played down the prospect.

Perez, 79, secured another four-year term in June after Real’s first contested presidential election in two decades.

More ‌than ‌a third of voting members backed challenger Enrique Riquelme, who opposed plans to bring outside investment into the member-owned club.

articles.title: Zverev cae en un debut trampa ante Musetti y se despide de París
articles.standfirst: El alemán, que dominaba el primer tie-break por 5-2, acaba cediendo en dos sets
articles.summary: El alemán, que dominaba el primer tie-break por 5-2, acaba cediendo en dos sets
articles.body: París ya no podrá disfrutar del campeón de 2024. Alexander Zverev, recién ascendido al número 1 del mundo, ha cedido en su debut en el Masters 1000 galo por 7-6 (5) y 6-2 ante el italiano Lorenzo Musetti. Hoy Sascha tenía enfrente un debut trampa ante el italiano, que está pasando por su mejor momento de la temporada con el título conseguido hace dos semanas en Lyon. Es el primero que levanta tras más de cuatro años de espera. En París ya acumula dos victorias de mérito. Ante el polaco Hubert Hurkacz y la reciente frente al campeón de dos grandes, Alexander Zverev. Es la segunda vez que el de Carrera se lleva un duelo ante un jugador que ocupa el primer puesto del ranking ATP. La primera fue ante Novak Djokovic en Montecarlo 2023. El alemán no estaba firmando un mal partido. No tenía el día con su servicio, pero salvaba las situaciones. Llegados al desempate inicial, Sascha comenzó mandando con mucha seguridad. Firmaba un 5-2 para posteriormente tener la opción de cerrarlo con dos servicios. Pero no fue así. Los fantasmas del pasado aparecieron, y un inspirado Musetti le dio la vuelta. Zverev no firmó ningún punto más en el tie-break. La segunda manga ya estaba decidida antes de empezar. El teutón salvó una bola de rotura en el juego inicial pero ya se le veía otra cara. Cabizbajo y sin intentar darle la vuelta, Musetti firmó el 'break' con 1-1 y eso le llevó hacia la tercera ronda del último TMS de la temporada. Sascha, por primera vez en dos años, ya que ganó en 2024 y fue semifinalista en 2025, disfrutará de más tiempo de descanso de cara a la Copa de Maestros de Turín (15 al 22). Una cita siempre marcada en rojo en el calendario del alemán. Ya ganó dos veces allí. En 2018 ante Djokovic y 2021 frente a Medvedev. Tras esto, le quedará la 'Final a 8' de la Copa Davis en Bolonia (24 al 29).

images.caption: Zverev al final del partido. LAPRESSE

articles.title: La derrota de De Miñaur mantiene vivas las esperanzas de las ATP Finals para Jódar
articles.standfirst: El australiano cae ante Etcheverry y ya queda por debajo del madrileño en la 'race'
articles.summary: El australiano cae ante Etcheverry y ya queda por debajo del madrileño en la 'race'
articles.body: Ha saltado la sopresa en París. Tras el bombazo de la eliminación de Alexander Zverev, ha venido el de Alex de Miñaur. Pero este contiene buenas noticias para Rafa Jódar. El madrileño necesitaba sí o sí una derrota hoy de De Miñaur ante Tomas Etcheverry, y la ha conseguido. El argentino ha firmado la hazaña sobre la pista 2 de la Défense Arena de París por 7-6 (2) y 6-3 en favor de los intereses del recién ascendido al top10. Con el australiano fuera del camino, ya que tiene menos puntos que Jódar en la 'race' (3.234 acumula el español por los 3.170 de Alex), tan solo unas semifinales de Novak Djokovic y Taylor Fritz, y una final de Tommy Paul dejarían fuera a Rafa de las Nitto ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22). El serbio, que ocupa el decimoprimer puesto en la carrera a Turín con 2.940 puntos, está disputando su partido de segunda ronda ante el australiano Hijikata. Taylor Fritz, el primer americano en discordia con 2.900 puntos, jugará ante Molcan su segundo partido del torneo. En el caso de Tommy Paul, quien suma 2.825 puntos, ya está en la tercera ronda del TMS galo tras derrotar en 49 minutos a Dani Mérida.
